documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd reported its Q4 and full year FY26 financial and operational performance, achieving a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and strong gross refining margins. Management highlighted robust performance in distillate yields, value-added niche products, and successful energy efficiency initiatives. The company's debt-to-equity ratio improved significantly, supported by healthy cash flows, and the board recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year. Looking ahead, management remains focused on executing growth and capex projects including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets while navigating global uncertainties. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd reported a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY25 and Q4 crude throughput of 2.974 MMT, achieving strong operational reliability despite scheduled maintenance.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market has a clear shortfall in motor spirit (MS) where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand growth projections in the southern market are projected at 4% to 5% for MS and 3% for HSD.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has approved Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS projects requiring INR 1,600 crores and project execution is underway in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: Retail outlet endeavor licensing has started with 300 licenses taken and commissioning expected during FY26-27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The planned capex for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project is INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project is INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Total capital expenditure spent during the financial year was Rs. 673 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: Maintenance capex is expected to remain in the Rs. 200 to Rs. 250 crore range.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new CBR refinery capacity will be 9 million metric tons with a petrochemical intensity of 6% for polypropylene.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for quarter 4 was $10.3 per barrel.
Foreign exchange loss for the quarter was approximately INR 200 crores and for the whole year around INR 350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full-year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel or Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss came down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.
margins_costs.quote: and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: The full-year inventory resulted in a loss of $0.06 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM was $12.94 per barrel in 2022-23, $8.21 per barrel in 2023-24, and $3.75 per barrel in 9M 2024-25.
Singapore GRM was reported as $10.70 per barrel in 2022-23, $6.58 per barrel in 2023-24, and $4.02 per barrel in 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved its highest ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, the company achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput achieved for the year was 10.45 MMT, which is equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Quarter 4 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The Manali Refinery has an installed capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR 1,900 crores and net borrowings at INR 973 crores, resulting in a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: Capital expenditure for the year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Debt-to-equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as on March 31, 2025, compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: Borrowings were Rs. 4,236 crore in 2022-23, Rs. 2,762 crore in 2023-24, and Rs. 5,700 crore in 9M 2024-25.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations and earnings.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the INR 2,000 crores total capex for LOBS and retail outlets will happen over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Normal maintenance capex is assumed at another INR 500 crores every year.
management_commitments.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the normal maintenance capex for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
